newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Cambodia calls for help to rid itself of landmines.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia calls for help to rid itself of landmines.

text.p: Cambodia's foreign minister on Tuesday appealed for help in ridding his country of its 4 million landmines, saying the world should outlaw the production, export, use and sale of mines as soon as possible.
In his speech to the General Assembly, Ung Huot said there were more landmines in Cambodia than nearly any other nation in the world.

"How many millions of these cold, cruel and silent enemies still await our unsuspecting and innocent civilian population in remote areas of the country near the western border?" he asked. "Banning them is an easy job. We need international support to fully eradicate them."
He said states needed to take action to outlaw as soon as possible "the production, exportation, utilization and the sale of mines."

A U.N.-sponsored conference in Geneva agreed to limit the use of some landmines in May, but stopped short of a ban because some countries argue they should remain a legitimate form of military defence.

Huot also said that developing nations, like his own, have have seen little recovery in the world economy during the past four years and were vulnerable to the free flow of capital over national borders.
"For many poorer nations, this has resulted in increased national debt burdens with the consequence of greater instability in the daily lives of their citizens," he said.
